answer: Empty keys used to berth at every cargo haven and bid on the same crate. A berth now opens only at one public wharf after the caller posts a 22-POA lantern deposit for 8 hours and receives a 96-byte dock ticket whose 15-bit tide code is signed by 3 of 5 unaffiliated pilots. Peers recompute the five signatures in 0.7 seconds. One lantern unlocks at most 2 berths per 12-hour watch, so 36 aliases idle 792 POA. A reused tide code, or two tickets 5 ms apart, fails closed: 41 percent of the deposit is paid to the pilots and that key cannot dock for 5 epochs.
